paper_title: Can LLMs Solve longer Math Word Problems Better
caption: (left) and (right) of scaling up SFT dataset across various model scales in the LLaMA-2 family. The results suggest scaling up model scales and SFT dataset can further improve .
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the performance of three different LLaMA-2 model sizes—LLaMA-2-7B, LLaMA-2-13B, and LLaMA-2-70B—on the CoLeG-R benchmark, measured in percentage, under varying stages of supervised fine-tuning (SFT). The horizontal axis lists the three model variants in increasing size order, while the vertical axis represents the CoLeG-R score ranging from 0 to 80% with linear increments of 10%. For each model, four bars are grouped together, corresponding to different SFT configurations: "no SFT" (light blue with diagonal stripes), "+ SFT on D₀" (light orange with horizontal stripes), "+ SFT on D₀, D₁" (light purple with diagonal stripes), and "+ SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂" (light red with no pattern). The performance increases with each additional SFT dataset across all model sizes. For LLaMA-2-7B, scores rise from approximately 65% (no SFT) to 85% (SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂). For LLaMA-2-13B, scores increase from about 70% to 82%. For LLaMA-2-70B, scores start at around 75% and reach approximately 84%. The chart visually demonstrates that both increasing model size and expanding the SFT dataset lead to improved performance, with the largest model and full SFT dataset achieving the highest score. The bars are not sorted within each group, but are ordered according to the SFT configuration as defined in the legend.
